title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the 4th draft of the 'Analysis situs' chapter (1986), Grothendieck builds a combinatorial, tame topology of 'polyhedra' and 'figures' inside a totally ordered set L. Here M = M_0 ⊔ M_1, where M_0 are points and M_1 are open intervals S_{a,b}. A figure 𝔏 ⊂ M is a finite set of points and open intervals, and this page treats the 1-dimensional case. The preceding page classified the vertices of such a figure into five combinatorial types: isolated; boundary proper; boundary improper; interior proper (redundant, 'de morcellement'); interior improper (lacunary).

On this page he defines a canonical reduction 𝔏 ↦ Ψ = 𝔏_comp in three steps.
(i) Take the closure 𝔏̄ (the 'figure associated to 𝔏').
(ii) Remove its isolated points, giving 𝔏̄ \ 𝔏̄_is, the purely 1-dimensional closure.
(iii) 'Compose' adjacent intervals by erasing redundant interior points.

The result Ψ has connected components that are closed segments. It is therefore encoded by a finite chain D = {X_1 <_1 X_2 <_1 ... <_1 X_n} in (M_1, <_1). Here X_i = S_{a_i,b_i}, and X <_1 Y means X lies entirely to the left of Y. Then Ψ = 𝔏_D and ∂Ψ = {a_1, b_1, ..., a_n, b_n}.

He then asks what extra data recovers 𝔏 from Ψ. Step 1 is a finite chain (flag) Δ in L containing ∂Ψ. Its new points (marked × in the figure) are the isolated vertices and the interior vertices of 𝔏.

The next page continues the decomposition:
- Δ = ∂Ψ ⊔ Δ_int ⊔ Δ_is, where Δ_int = Δ ∩ interior of the shadow Omb(Ψ).
- Δ_int = Δ_lac ⊔ Δ_red.
- A subset ∂_0 ⊂ ∂Ψ records which endpoints actually belong to 𝔏.

Together these give a normal form, a bijective parametrisation, of finite 'constructible' subsets of a linear order: a disjoint union of segments plus marked points, each labelled by its type. The purpose is presumably to enumerate or classify figures combinatorially, as groundwork for a tame / o-minimal-style dimension theory.
errors: Notation clash: ∂𝔏 is set equal to ∂Ψ = {a_i, b_i}. If ∂ meant the topological frontier of 𝔏, it would also contain isolated points and lacunary interior points. So ∂ here must mean 'endpoints of the 1-dimensional hull', and the equality ∂Ψ = ∂𝔏 holds only under that convention.

The definition of 𝔏_comp leaves implicit that erasing redundant points is done after taking the closure. Lacunary points of 𝔏 (missing interior points) also disappear in the closure, so both redundant and lacunary interior points are lost. The page's statement that 'new points of Δ are the isolated and interior vertices' is consistent with this.
Minor point: the formula is written with a stray '=' ('Δ δ𝔏 = ∈ Drap*(L)'), a slip of the pen.

ideas.what: Canonical reduction of a finite figure in a linear order: closure, remove isolated points, merge adjacent intervals. Encoding of the result by a chain of disjoint intervals.
ideas.modern_name: normal form of definable/constructible subsets of a dense linear order (o-minimal dimension 1, cell decomposition); interval-union normal form
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; o-minimal cell decomposition (van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight 1980s)
ideas.where_published: Only the general programme of 'topologie modérée' appears, in the Esquisse d'un programme (1984).

ideas.what: Reconstruction of a figure from its compacted hull plus a marked flag Δ ⊃ ∂Ψ, with a typed partition of vertices (boundary proper/improper, interior redundant/lacunary, isolated).
ideas.modern_name: combinatorial encoding / stratification data of a 1-dimensional constructible set

deep.surprise_reason: This is careful but elementary bookkeeping: a normal form for finite unions of points and intervals in a line. It is a foundational detail of Grothendieck's tame-topology draft, with no new result or unexpected connection.
transcription_corrections: The crossed-out word before 'composition' reads like 'télescopée' (the 'télescopage' idea), replaced by 'composition'. The subscript under 𝔏 at the top right is 'comp'.
The marginal note on the left reads 'marqués par une ×', attached by an asterisk to 'pts marqués*' in the last line.
The last line reads approximately: 'les nouveaux pts marqués* correspondant aux sommets isolés et les sommets intérieurs de 𝔏'; the crossed-out word is 'points'.
The page number in the archive is 121; Grothendieck's own numbering is 112.
